extracted.intended_audience: Authors, editors, reviewers, and readers of qualitative research (especially in health and medical education)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and checklist (SRQR) for transparent reporting of qualitative research manuscripts to guide authors in manuscript preparation and assist editors and reviewers in evaluation. Covers title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and other disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise description of the nature and topic of the study; identifying the study as qualitative or indicating the approach or data collection methods is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the study as qualitative or indicate the approach (e.g., ethnography, grounded theory) or data collection methods (e.g., interview, focus group). The title should concisely describe the nature and topic of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of key elements of the study using the abstract format of the intended publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically includes background, purpose, methods, results, and conclusions; results reported narratively rather than numerically and authors rarely present a specific hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Description and significance of the problem/phenomenon studied; review of relevant theory and empirical work; problem statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the problem/phenomenon is important and situate it in relevant theory and prior empirical research to justify the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose or research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the study and specific objectives or questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear study purposes or research questions that guide the qualitative inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative approach and research paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative approach (e.g., ethnography, grounded theory, case study, phenomenology, narrative research) and guiding theory if appropriate; identifying the research paradigm is also recommended; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the chosen qualitative approach and paradigm (e.g., postpositivist, constructivist/interpretivist), provide a rationale discussing why that approach/theory was chosen over alternatives, and describe assumptions and limitations implicit in those choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher characteristics and reflexivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers' characteristics that may influence the research, including personal attributes, qualifications/experience, relationship with participants, assumptions, and/or presuppositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe potential or actual interaction between researchers' characteristics and the research questions, approach, methods, results, and/or transferability; make assumptions and perspectives explicit (reflexivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting/site and salient contextual factors; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the study setting and context factors important to understanding the findings and transferability; explain why the chosen context matters for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: How and why research participants, documents, or events were selected; criteria for deciding when no further sampling was necessary (e.g., sampling saturation); rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain selection criteria, sampling procedures, and stopping rules (e.g., how saturation was defined and recognized) and justify choices relative to the study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues pertaining to human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of approval by an appropriate ethics review board and participant consent, or explanation for lack thereof; other confidentiality and data security issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ethical approvals, consent processes, confidentiality measures, and data security considerations; explain exceptions if ethics approval or consent was not obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of data collected; details of data collection procedures including start and stop dates, iterative process, triangulation of sources/methods, and modification of procedures in response to evolving study findings; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data collection in sufficient detail (including timelines, iteration, triangulation, and procedural modifications) so readers understand how data were gathered and why methods were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection instruments and technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of instruments (e.g., interview guides, questionnaires) and devices (e.g., audio recorders) used for data collection; if/how the instrument(s) changed over the course of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide instruments or their descriptions, note technological tools used, and explain any changes to instruments during the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of study
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and relevant characteristics of participants, documents, or events included in the study; level of participation (could be reported in results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size and participant or unit characteristics relevant to interpretation (e.g., demographics, roles); clarify degree of participation and inclusion/exclusion details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for processing data prior to and during analysis, including transcription, data entry, data management and security, verification of data integrity, data coding, and anonymization/deidentification of excerpts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures used to prepare raw data for analysis (transcription protocols, data management systems, coding files), processes to ensure data integrity, and steps taken to anonymize or deidentify data excerpts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Process by which inferences, themes, etc., were identified and developed, including the researchers involved in data analysis; usually references a specific paradigm or approach; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain analytic procedures (e.g., coding, thematic development, constant comparison), name who was involved, reference analytic frameworks/paradigms, and provide rationale for chosen analytic strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques to enhance trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques to enhance trustworthiness and credibility of data analysis (e.g., member checking, audit trail, triangulation); rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report strategies used to bolster credibility and trustworthiness (member checks, reflexive journals, multiple coders, audit trails, triangulation), justify chosen techniques, and describe how they were implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Main findings (e.g., interpretations, inferences, and themes); might include development of a theory or model, or integration with prior research or theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present main analytic findings clearly, including interpretive claims, thematic structures, conceptual models, or theories generated; link interpretations to the analytic process and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to empirical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence (e.g., quotes, field notes, text excerpts, photographs) to substantiate analytic findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide illustrative empirical data (participant quotes, excerpts, field notes, images) that substantiate claims and allow readers to judge the fit between data and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with prior work, implications, transferability, and contribution(s) to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Short summary of main findings; explanation of how findings and conclusions connect to, support, elaborate on, or challenge conclusions of earlier scholarship; discussion of scope of application/generalizability; identification of unique contribution(s) to scholarship in a discipline or field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how results relate to existing literature and theory, implications for practice or research, the scope and boundaries (transferability) of the findings, and the study's unique contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustworthiness and limitations of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe study limitations, threats to trustworthiness, and how these limitations affect interpretation and transferability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential sources of influence or perceived influence on study conduct and conclusions; how these were managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any potential conflicts or influences and describe steps taken to manage or mitigate their impact on study conduct, analysis, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding and other support; role of funders in data collection, interpretation, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and other support and explicitly state the funders' role (or lack of role) in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, writing, and publication decisions.
